brief: A wall-hung spice rack: at least three bins, hung from keyhole hangers.

requirements.evidence: Three full-depth bins: bin:-1,0,0~hex-bin-full, bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full, bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full, one in each of the three hex cells.

Two hex-acc-keyhole accessories fitted to the outer cells: accessory:0#-1,0#1 and accessory:0#1,0#1 (slot 1 on each end cell), so the rack lifts onto and drops over wall screws; note the configurator checks fit only, not load rating of the hangers.

Each bin staged with a glass-tumbler prop standing in it, visible from above (look polar 10). No dedicated spice-jar prop exists in the catalogue, so tumblers stand in to show jar storage; the bins themselves are the storage.

finish.summary: A wall-hung spice rack: three full hex cells in a row, each with a full-depth bin (3 bins total), one group locked with joint bolts and open faces capped. Two keyhole hangers (hex-acc-keyhole) on the end cells let it drop onto wall screws. Each bin is staged with a small tumbler to show jar storage in use (no spice-jar prop exists). check_build is clean with meshClash clear.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
